newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler sees lower 1997 U.S. industry sales.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler sees lower 1997 U.S. industry sales.

text.p: Chrysler Corp Chairman Robert Eaton said Thursday that the automaker continues to expect U.S. industry vehicle sales in 1997 to reach about 15.2 million cars and trucks.
That represents a slight drop from the approximately 15.4 million vehicles automakers sold in the 1996 calendar year.

"We expect 1997 to be a good year for the economy as well as for our industry with sales forecast at 15.2 million vehicles in the U.S., including medium and heavy duty trucks," Eaton said in a statement.

"We believe inflation will be held in check, interest rates should remain stable and the economy should continue its moderate growth at just under 2.5 percent," Eaton said. "We also believe, unfortunately, the dollar will continue to be overvalued for most of all of the year but both gasoline prices and oil prices will likely drop by year-end."
Eaton said the company's goal for 1997 is to remain focused on controlling its costs and continually improving processes and products.
Chrysler increased its share of the U.S. car and light truck market to 15.9 percent through November, up from 14.3 percent in 1995 and 12 percent in 1991.

Chrysler Chief Economist Van Bussmann said the automaker anticipates further increases in market share in 1997, but has set no specific goals. The company will receive full production of redesigned Jeep Cherokee and Wrangler models, as well as the Dodge Dakota pickup truck. It also will introduce a new sport/utility vehicle based on the Dakota -- the Dodge Durango -- as well as a new generation of its LH family sedans.
